reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection preserves the target input rows required for the downstream recommendation. The visible function selects rows with demand_score >= 3 while retaining the explicit fallback ids, and the supplied output contains all eight corpus records without introducing unrelated candidates. The package does not include underlying market-demand narratives beyond scored needs, so strict customer-demand substantiation cannot be independently re-established here; it is not a localized defect in this boundary given the declared input contract.

evidence_normalization retains the selected records whose record_id values are in the allowed set and applies the declared bounded index window of eight rows. The upstream output shows all eight normalized needs preserved, including the high-priority n06-r01 record that drives the deterministic downstream recommendation. No contradictory or missing handoff evidence is visible for this boundary.

provenance_assembly deterministically ranks normalized needs by descending demand_score with record_id as the tie-breaker and assembles the evidence_sources handoff records. The supplied upstream output ranks n06-r01 first and preserves all eight source records; the runtime handoff metadata also shows exact hash agreement for both needs and evidence_sources handoffs. No behaviorally significant fault is localized to this boundary.
